Alex —

Great to hear and congrats on the close. Attached is a draft MAP that embeds the evaluation plan, a shadow-canary runbook, and a draft training schedule. High-level callouts below and next steps:

1) MAP summary (one pager in attached PDF)
   - Phase A (Week 0–2): Prep + configs (KMS, VPC peering, SLA routing rules).
   - Phase B (Week 3–4): Shadow canary — mirror 10% of production read traffic; no writes. Warm KV cache + tokenization sanity checks.
   - Phase C (Week 5): Controlled lift (migration window) — weekend cutover option; index sync + final cache priming.
   - Phase D (Week 6–8): Post-cut monitoring + training rotations + rollback guardrails.

2) Evaluation plan (embedded in MAP) — pass/fail gates we propose
   - Functional parity: sample of 1,000 representative requests compared against baseline model responses; threshold: >= 98% acceptance by your product QA team.
   - Latency SLO: p95 under our configured target for the reserved pool. If p95 exceeds target by >20% over 30m, pause rollout.
   - Quality regression: run our automated eval harness on your golden prompts daily during the mirror run; critical regressions trigger an emergency rollback.

3) Canary run details
   - Mode: Shadow (mirror) first 2 weeks; Day-2 metrics collection and alert tuning on day 3.
   - Traffic shaping: start at 1% mirrored, step to 10% by day 3 if metrics stable.
   - KV cache warmup plan: pre-warm top 5K prefixes nightly during shadow.

4) Training + ops handoff
   - Two 3-hour sessions (Platform team + App team) covering runtime config, rollback playbook, and observability dashboards.
   - Recording + runbook will be uploaded to the Drive link in the MAP.

5) Rollback and fallback
   - Automatic fallback to hosted model variant if model memory/throughput alarms exceed thresholds.
   - Manual rollback criteria outlined in runbook (attached xlsx).

Next steps: please confirm the preferred 2-week window in June/July for shadow run and the team members for training cohorts.

I copied Karthik and Monica for technical details and scheduling.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.ai

Alex / Lauren — quick technical clarifications and a proposed canary cadence:

- Mirror method: we will use asynchronous mirror with header tagging so your telemetry pipeline can distinguish mirrored requests. No downstream write calls will be forwarded.
- Evaluation harness: we propose an initial delta-run comparing output embeddings + tokenized output length. For quality we will provide a daily regression report and a detailed example set on failures.
- Canary cadence proposal:
    Week 1: 1% mirror (sanity) -> collect baseline logs and fix any alert noise.
    Week 2: 10% mirror -> run full eval harness nightly.

- Migration notes: if you opt for lift-and-shift indices, we recommend a cold sync on Fri night and a warm sync Saturday morning, then a controlled route switch Sunday 02:00–04:00 PT. We'll staff an on-call infra engineer for those windows.

Action items for Finacore:
- Confirm mirror start date (we are tentatively holding 2026-06-28 to 2026-07-11).
- Provide list of 12 golden prompts for the initial eval set.

I added specific runbook steps in the attached xlsx (playbook tab).

—Karthik
